parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence; foreign passports accepted on ordinary terms (90-day visa-free); no facility, bathroom or screening restriction documented for visitors. The documented visitor-facing exposure is one custody case (2024): a trans foreign national placed in a male detention centre with HRT interrupted three months — but NGO intervention secured release, and a 2024 human-rights court ruling established that medication denial is litigable and compensable, so recourse partly works. Hate-crime law omits gender identity, a real recourse gap, though a prosecutorial response team exists. Hostility signals (LGBT-free-zone legacy, 2019 march violence, presidential rhetoric) are largely LGBT-wide, dated, or resident-facing; courts annulled the resolutions. Civil society is active and the 2025 LGR reform improves institutional climate. Documented friction, custody uncertainty, and a hate-crime coverage gap hold it at reduced risk near the lower edge of that band.
